title: Power-series rings over fields or Cohen rings are adically formally smooth over the prime ring
statement: Let $n\ge0$. If $K$ is a field of characteristic zero and $S=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], then $S$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ for its maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. If $K$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$ and $S=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$, then $S$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf F_p$ for its maximal-ideal-adic topology. If $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $S=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$, then $S$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Z$ for its maximal-ideal-adic topology (the maximal ideal being $(p,X_1,\ldots,X_n)$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs), all three clauses and proof using Algebra Proposition Tag 0322 and Lemma Tag 0329

proof.text: *Clauses (1) and (3).* Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $S=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring] for the local ring $K$ (maximal ideal $0$), $S$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S=\{F:F(0)=0\}$; this is the ideal $(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$, since a series with zero constant term is $\sum_iX_iF_i$ where $F_i$ collects (divided by $X_i$) the monomials whose first variable with positive exponent is $X_i$, and conversely every $X_iF$ has zero constant term. So $S$ and $\mathfrak m_S$ are $C$ and $\mathfrak m_C=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ of part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-cohen-formally-smooth-adic] (with $x_i=X_i$), which says that $S$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ for the $\mathfrak m_S$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let $\Lambda$ be a Cohen ring with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] (so of residue characteristic $p$) and $S=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring] for the local ring $\Lambda$, $\mathfrak m_S=\{F:F(0)\in p\Lambda\}$, which is $(p,X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ by the same decomposition $F=F(0)+\sum_iX_iF_i$. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-cohen-formally-smooth-adic] says that $S$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Z$ for this $\mathfrak m_S$-adic topology. This proves the first and third assertions. (Source: 07NL, clauses (1) and (3), reduced in the source to $\mathbf Q\to K$ formally smooth, Proposition 0322, and $\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$ formally smooth for the $p$-adic topology, Lemma 0329; both are carried in the cited node.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL, clauses (1) and (3) and the proof (lines 9718-9731)

proof.text: *Clause (2): the test datum.* Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ and $S=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], an $\mathbf F_p$-algebra through $\mathbf F_p\subseteq K\subseteq S$; as in Step 1 ([lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring] for the local ring $K$), $\mathfrak m_S=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$. By [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] we must show: given a commutative ring $D$ with a ring map $\mathbf F_p\to D$, an ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, the quotient map $q:D\to D/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and a homomorphism of $\mathbf F_p$-algebras $g:S\to D/J$ with $g(\mathfrak m_S^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$, there is a homomorphism of $\mathbf F_p$-algebras $f:S\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. Fix such data. Since $\mathbf F_p\to D$ is a ring map, $p\cdot1_D=0$; and every ring homomorphism between rings $E,E'$ with $p\cdot1_E=0=p\cdot1_{E'}$ is a homomorphism of $\mathbf F_p$-algebras, because there is only one ring map $\mathbf F_p\to E'$ ($n\bmod p\mapsto n\cdot1_{E'}$). Since $q$ is surjective choose $d_i\in D$ with $q(d_i)=g(X_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,n$. As $X_i^k\in\mathfrak m_S^k$, $q(d_i^k)=g(X_i^k)=0$, so $d_i^k\in J$ and $d_i^{2k}\in J^2=0$. Let $\mathfrak a=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\subseteq D$ and $M=n(2k-1)+1$. A product of $M$ of the generators $d_1,\ldots,d_n$ contains some $d_i$ at least $2k$ times (pigeonhole), hence is $0$; so $\mathfrak a^M=0$, and $\bar{\mathfrak a}^M=q(\mathfrak a^M)=0$ for $\bar{\mathfrak a}=q(\mathfrak a)\subseteq D/J$ (for $n=0$, $\mathfrak a=0$ and $M=1$). A ring $T$ with an ideal $\mathfrak b$ such that $\mathfrak b^M=0$ is $\mathfrak b$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]: for $m\ge M$, $T/\mathfrak b^m=T$ and the transition maps are the identity, so $T\to\varprojlim_mT/\mathfrak b^m$ is injective and every compatible family is the image of its component in $T/\mathfrak b^M=T$. Hence $D$ is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete, $D/J$ is $\bar{\mathfrak a}$-adically complete, $d_i\in\mathfrak a$ and $g(X_i)=q(d_i)\in\bar{\mathfrak a}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL clause (2); the reduction 'by the universal property of power series rings' (line 9719), written out

proof.text: *Clause (2): lifting on the coefficients.* The restriction $g|_K:K\to D/J$ is a ring homomorphism, $D$ satisfies $p\cdot1_D=0$ (Step 2) and $J^2=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-nilpotent-lifting] for the field $K$ of characteristic $p$, with $N=2$, applied to $D$, $J$, $\pi=q$ and $g|_K$, there is a ring homomorphism $h:K\to D$ with $q\circ h=g|_K$. (This is the formal smoothness of $\mathbf F_p\to K$, which the source takes from Algebra, Proposition Tag 0322: $\mathbf F_p$ is perfect, so $K/\mathbf F_p$ is separable, hence formally smooth.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NL, item (2) of the reduction: 'F_p -> L is formally smooth' and 'The first two are Algebra, Proposition 0322' (lines 9722, 9727-9729)

proof.text: *Clause (2): extension to the power series ring.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to $\Lambda=K$, $T=D$ (which is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete by Step 2), $\alpha=h$ (Step 3) and $t_i=d_i\in\mathfrak a$: there is a ring homomorphism $f:S\to D$ with $f|_K=h$ and $f(X_i)=d_i$. The two ring homomorphisms $q\circ f$ and $g$ from $S$ to $D/J$ agree on $K$ ($q\circ h=g|_K$) and send each $X_i$ to $q(d_i)=g(X_i)\in\bar{\mathfrak a}$; by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] for $\Lambda=K$, $T=D/J$ (which is $\bar{\mathfrak a}$-adically complete by Step 2), $\alpha=g|_K$ and $t_i=g(X_i)$, we get $q\circ f=g$. By Step 2 ($p\cdot1_S=0$, $p\cdot1_D=0$) the ring homomorphism $f$ is a homomorphism of $\mathbf F_p$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NL: 'By the universal property of power series rings it suffices to prove' (line 9719)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* For every test datum $(D,J,g,k)$ of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $\mathbf F_p\to S=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ and the ideal $\mathfrak m_S$, Steps 2-4 give a homomorphism of $\mathbf F_p$-algebras $f:S\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$; so $S$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf F_p$ for the $\mathfrak m_S$-adic topology. With Step 1 this proves all three assertions.
